conceptual assets.reasoning: Sequencer process: when rstn_ext_i = '0' the code clears sreg_ext and drives rstn_ext_o <= '0'; on rising_edge(clk_i) it shifts sreg_ext <= sreg_ext(sreg_ext'left-1 downto 0) & '1' and drives rstn_ext_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_ext). The module therefore computes a filtered/synchronized external-reset-release value; the correctness of that produced value is established by these RTL relations (Integrity). sreg_ext implements the stored shift state and rstn_ext_o is the entity exit through which the decision leaves.

Sequencer process: on rstn_ext_i = '0' the process clears sreg_sys; on rising_edge(clk_i) it clears sreg_sys if (rstn_wdt_i = '0') or (rstn_dbg_i = '0') else shifts sreg_sys <= sreg_sys(sreg_sys'left-1 downto 0) & '1', and drives rstn_sys_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_sys). The RTL thus implements a gated, shift-register-based system-reset release; integrity of rstn_sys_o/sreg_sys is established by these assignments and gating conditions.

Synchronizer process: if rstn_ext_i = '0' then xrstn_wdt_o <= '0' else on rising_edge(clk_i) the process assigns xrstn_wdt_o <= rstn_wdt_i. The entity therefore produces a clocked, synchronized copy of the watchdog-reset input; the RTL establishes that xrstn_wdt_o must match that synchronized relation (Integrity).

Synchronizer process: if rstn_ext_i = '0' then xrstn_ocd_o <= '0' else on rising_edge(clk_i) it assigns xrstn_ocd_o <= rstn_dbg_i. The RTL thus implements a clocked synchronized copy of the debug-reset input; integrity of xrstn_ocd_o relative to that assignment is established by the code.

conceptual assets.concept: Clock-divider enable pulses (clk_en_o) produced from internal counters
conceptual assets.reasoning: Ticker process: on rstn_i = '0' the RTL clears en, cnt and cnt2; on rising_edge(clk_i) it sets en <= or_reduce_f(enable_i), increments cnt when en = '1' (cnt <= unsigned(cnt)+1) and copies cnt2 <= cnt. The code then drives clk_en_o bits as e.g. cnt(n) and (not cnt2(n)). This implements single-cycle enable pulses derived from counter bit rises; the correctness of clk_en_o (and of the counters/en that realize it) is established by these RTL relations (Integrity).
